subject: HighTide private cluster — sudden p95 increase and spike in 5xx

Subject: Production latency & 5xx spike — private deployment

Jordan —

We're seeing a sharp regression on our private VPC deployment starting ~08:45 PT: p95 tail went from ~220ms to ~1.4s, and 5xx errors climbed from 0.2% to ~6% over the last 30m. No config changes on our side; we did push a model refresh yesterday evening but that was a small tokenizer tweak.

Attached is a small log bundle (hightide-support-log-20270530.zip). Can you help triage? This is affecting checkout flows for a subset of customers.

Alex
Lead SRE, HighTide Logistics

Subject: Fwd: Production latency & 5xx spike — private deployment

Forwarding from HighTide. They report a big p95 jump and 5xx spike on their private cluster (deployed in us-west-2). They rolled a model refresh yesterday; customer says it was small. Key asks: urgent triage, short-term mitigation (reduce customer impact), and if needed we escalate to execs for credits/extra capacity.

Immediate asks:
- Can we get a profiler snapshot and top-level metrics (gpu_util, queue depth, batch sizes) for that customer's cluster?
- Any recent kernel or runtime changes pushed to the private agent in the last 48h?

Looping Marissa/Michael/Neha for triage.

Thanks,
Jordan
Account Exec — Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 09:48:03 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production latency & 5xx spike — private deployment

Quick triage notes:
- I pulled the customer's route: recent traffic pattern shows larger short-lived bursts (checkout storms) which will naturally increase batching queues and p95.
- No infra agent updates in the last 48h for their cluster according to the control plane.

Short-term mitigations to propose to customer (low-risk, reversible):
1) Reduce target_max_batch_size for their route from 64 -> 16 to limit tail latency. Expect lower throughput but improved p95.
2) Enable prefix/KV warmup for the high-traffic routes for 30 minutes to populate KV cache.
3) If they accept, we can spin +1 dedicated small GPU (burst capacity) for 2 hours to drain backlog.

I'll start a profiler capture (30s) and request the runtime logs. Neha — can you issue the profiler and share output? Michael — can you validate whether quantized variant v1.2 is safe for them (we onboarded yesterday).

Marissa
Solutions Eng — Redwood Inference
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 10:10:27 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production latency & 5xx spike — private deployment

Checked the model variants: v1.2 (int8 quant) was promoted yesterday but should be functionally equivalent; still, quantized variants can increase CPU/GPU memory pressure in some edge sequences. Two quick things I recommend now: 

1) Immediate: Add a transient routing policy to prefer the unquantized model for 15 minutes for routes showing >1% error. This is an automated partial rollback we can trigger from control plane.
2) Short-term config: set target_max_batch_size=16 and max_wait_ms=25 to limit batching latency.
3) SRE action: if p95 stays >800ms after 20m, request capacity burst (+1 GPU) and enable KV warming.

I'm OK with the quantized fallback plan — any impact on cost we can reconcile later. I will check the runtime logs for OOMs or kernel retries.

—Michael
Head of Runtime Engineering, Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 10:45:55 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production latency & 5xx spike — private deployment

Profiler and logs attached: profiler-sample-20270531.tar.gz, kvcache-heatmap.png. Findings: 
- Hotspots: kernel kernel_attn_batched and kv-lookup time increased ~3x at the time of spike.
- No OOMs; GPU util spikes correlated with queue depth surges.
- Several requests showed KV cache misses for cold prefixes (new checkout flows).

Immediate actions taken (15m window):
- Triggered model rollback preference to unquantized variant for impacted routes.
- Reduced target_max_batch_size to 16 and max_wait_ms to 25.
- Enabled KV warming for top 5 routes for 20 minutes.

Attaching artifacts for your review. I'll keep sampling for 2h.

Neha
SRE — Redwood Inference

Alex / Sunita —

Thanks for the quick heads-up and for sending logs. We've applied a few short-term mitigations and are continuing to monitor:
- Reduced batching (target_max_batch_size -> 16) and tightened max_wait_ms.
- Preferred unquantized model for impacted routes (auto rollback).
- Enabled KV warming for hot prefixes.

Preliminary numbers: 30m after changes p95 reduced to ~280-320ms and 5xxs fell to ~0.8%. We'll keep the burst capacity option open if you want additional headroom for the next 2 hours.

Would you like us to keep current mitigations for 24h while we run a deeper root-cause analysis and validate the quantized variant compatibility with your checkout traffic? If yes, we recommend a scheduled maintenance window tomorrow to test quantized variant with canary traffic and kernel tuning.

Jordan

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Leadership Distribution <leadership@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 17:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Exec summary: HighTide private cluster latency incident (May 30)

Team —

Summary (for execs):
- Impact: HighTide Logistics (one of our Top-30 accounts) experienced a p95 regression from ~220ms -> ~1.4s and a 5xx spike to ~6% on 2027-05-30 08:45 PT after they rolled a model refresh. Customer traffic pattern (checkout bursts) amplified batching pressure and KV cache cold-starts.
- Actions taken: transient rollback to unquantized model variant; reduced target_max_batch_size to 16; KV warming; profiler capture and runtime logs analyzed. Short-term mitigations restored p95 to ~280–320ms and reduced 5xx to ~0.8%.
- Root cause hypothesis: interaction between quantized kernel path and bursty sequence prefixes leading to increased KV lookup latency and queue depth at peak. No agent/kernel patch in the customer's cluster in last 48h.
- Recommended next steps (approval requested):
  1) Approve a 2-hour burst of +1 dedicated small GPU for the customer's cluster to eliminate drain risk during working hours. (Estimated incremental cost: $X/day; we can apply a discretionary credit as needed.)
  2) Schedule a controlled canary test of the quantized variant on a 5% traffic slice with kernel telemetry on Thu 2027-06-03.
  3) Engineering task: add a prioritization rule to reduce batch_size for short-sequence checkout routes to reduce tail latency as a permanent control.

Requested approvals: +1 dedicated GPU for 2 hours (yes/no), discretionary credit up to 10% of last month's bill (yes/no).

Attachments: incident artifacts in shared drive (JIRA-SUP-1298).

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Account Exec — Redwood Inference
